title: Expected squared chord distance for synchronously driven sphere diffusions
source_kind: Self-contained classical mathematical supplement; no novelty claim and no attribution to an external theorem number
status: Proposed pre-proof source/statement seal; not compiled or independently accepted
statement: Let N,d be natural numbers with N>0, E=R^d with its Euclidean inner product, S={x in E:||x||=1}, and C=S^N. Work on a probability space with a common complete right-continuous filtration. For each i<N let B_i be a standard E-valued Brownian motion relative to that filtration. Let X_i,Y_i be supplied jointly measurable strongly progressive S-valued processes. Fix lambda>=0. Let b_X,b_Y:[0,infinity) x C x C -> E^N be continuous. Suppose the displayed coordinate integral equations hold on every finite positive horizon, almost surely simultaneously at every time on that horizon and every particle/coordinate. Then the actual expected normalized squared chord distance satisfies the exact two-time integral balance below, is absolutely continuous on every finite interval, has the stated derivative at every positive time and the stated right derivative at time zero.

definitions.name: actual state and projection
definitions.body: E is EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), S is its literal norm-one subtype and C=Fin N -> S. P_x=I-x tensor x. Its jth column is e_j-x_j x. No intrinsic distance or projective quotient is used.

definitions.name: learning drifts
definitions.body: b_X(t,x,y)_i and b_Y(t,x,y)_i are the non-radial drift terms. Their sign is part of these functions. The full Ito drifts are b_X,i-lambda(d-1)x_i and b_Y,i-lambda(d-1)y_i. No separate tangency premise is required by this identity; the supplied solution is already S-valued.

definitions.name: same-driver coordinate equations
definitions.body: For each H>0, almost surely for every 0<=t<=H, i<N and k<d: X_i,k(t)=X_i,k(0)+integral_0^t [b_X(s,X(s),Y(s))_i,k-lambda(d-1)X_i,k(s)] ds + sum_j integral_0^t sqrt(2lambda)(1_{k=j}-X_i,j(s)X_i,k(s)) dB_i,j(s), and identically for Y with b_Y and Y. The SAME B_i,j occurs in the X and Y equations. The stochastic integral is the existing completed progressive L2 Ito integral, not an unconstrained symbol.

definitions.name: observables
definitions.body: delta_i(t)=X_i(t)-Y_i(t); D(t)=N^-1 sum_i E||delta_i(t)||^2; R4(t)=N^-1 sum_i E||delta_i(t)||^4; L(t)=2N^-1 sum_i E<delta_i(t), b_X(t,X(t),Y(t))_i-b_Y(t,X(t),Y(t))_i>. Set G(t)=L(t)-2lambda(d-3)D(t)-lambda R4(t). All expectations use the same original probability measure.

definitions.name: time and integrals
definitions.body: Process time is nonnegative real. D and G in the Lean real-time conclusion use t -> max(t,0), encoded by Real.toNNReal. The two-time integral is the oriented real Lebesgue interval integral. The derivative at zero is only relative to [0,infinity); no two-sided derivative across the constant negative-time extension is asserted.

definitions.name: filtration/Brownian convention
definitions.body: Usual conditions mean ambient probability-null sets belong to every time sigma algebra and the filtration is right-continuous. Each B_i starts at zero, has almost surely continuous paths and Gaussian identity-covariance independent increments, is strongly adapted, and future vector increments are independent of the entire past filtration. Scalar coordinate drivers are literal coordinates of B_i, not newly chosen unrelated Brownian motions.

assumptions.text: N is a positive natural number. d is a natural number. Supplied sphere-valued processes on a probability space make the d=0 empty-sphere case vacuous; no d>=3 hypothesis is needed for the exact identity.

One probability measure and one usual filtration; each B_i is standard relative to that common filtration. Independence of different B_i is not required for this average of separate squared distances. Both components of pair i share exactly B_i.

Each X_i,Y_i is jointly measurable in time/sample and strongly progressive. Whole-path continuity, initial measurability, square integrability of the projected noise, finite drift integrability and derivative-martingale centering are to be derived from the coordinate equations and compact continuous coefficients; they are not additional supplied hypotheses.

lambda is a fixed nonnegative real, including zero. Both non-radial fields are continuous jointly in time and all paired configurations. Their finite-horizon bounds come from compactness; no global-in-time bound or Lipschitz constant is assumed.

The exact supplied coordinate equations D3 hold for every positive horizon, outside one exceptional null set per horizon simultaneously for all its times and finite coordinates. This is the SDE premise, not an Ito formula for a nonlinear test function.

proof_inventory.detail: Compactness of C x C and continuity bound the drift fields. Existing bounded-progressive coefficient and sphere-noise constructors give the exact drift integrability and ProgressiveL2 noise representatives; adapted initial coordinates follow from strong progressivity.

proof_inventory.move: Use the existing actual compact Ito theorem
proof_inventory.detail: For each particle use the paired Euclidean state (X_i,Y_i), its common B_i coordinate family and the polynomial test f(x,y)=||x-y||^2. Its compact range is S x S. The derivative martingale is produced by the existing theorem. There is no new Ito proof or assumed quadratic-test balance.
The two blocks of the same noise column have difference sqrt(2lambda)(P_X-P_Y)e_j. The Hessian therefore gives 2lambda sum_j ||(P_X-P_Y)e_j||^2. Independent X/Y drivers would yield a different term.

proof_inventory.move: Retain exact radial and quartic terms
proof_inventory.detail: Use the unit-norm overlap identity and projection column norm calculation to obtain F3. After expectation the quartic is E||delta||^4. It is not replaced by the square of the second moment.
The actual derivative martingale starts at zero and has mean zero. Coefficients are bounded on finite horizons; use the existing expectation/time-integral balance and finite sums to obtain F1.

proof_inventory.move: Pointwise time conclusion from continuous coefficients
proof_inventory.detail: Derive continuous sample paths on each finite horizon from the supplied integral equations. Compact domination gives continuity of the expected generator. Reuse the existing continuous-generator weak-law FTC for positive times and its one-sided endpoint form at zero. This yields F2, rather than assuming differentiation under expectation.

boundaries.text: No process construction, pathwise uniqueness, invariant-law result, density existence, pointwise density PDE, stopped identity or global model theorem is claimed.
For d>=3 the radial/noise contribution is nonpositive. This sign is a downstream consequence; the exact identity itself does not need d>=3.

For a prescribed merely measurable locally bounded temperature, the analogous integral/absolutely-continuous/a.e.-derivative statement is a separate possible successor. This fixed-temperature unit neither assumes its pointwise differentiability nor claims it.

No independence of particle blocks is needed here. An empirical-feature quadratic variation with cross-particle terms is a different observable and needs its own driver independence/covariance argument.

The conclusion is a genuine stochastic observable identity. It does not instantiate every field of a downstream algebraic coupling certificate or discharge learning-force bounds, empirical variance bounds, or Gronwall hypotheses by wording.
